title: Purity of real lisse sheaves on curves
statement:
Let $C_0/\mathbf F_q$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve in the
sense of [d-real-setup] (not necessarily affine; e.g. proper) and let
$\mathcal G_0$ be a lisse
Weil sheaf on $C_0$ which is
$\iota$-real. Then every irreducible
constituent $\mathcal W$ of $\mathcal G_0$ (in the sense of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations]) is
punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $\dw_\iota(\mathcal W)$, its
determinant weight with
respect to $\iota$.

proof.text:
Step 0 (reduction to an affine curve). Punctual purity is a condition
at each closed point separately ([def-weil-punctual-weights]), so fix a
closed point $x$ of $C_0$ and an irreducible constituent $\mathcal W$
of $\mathcal G_0$, of rank $r$. Choose an affine open
$U_0\subseteq C_0$ containing $x$ (every point of a scheme has one). It
is again a smooth geometrically connected curve: $U=U_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}k$
is a nonempty open of the smooth connected, hence irreducible, curve
$C=C_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}k$, so it is connected. Let
$u:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be the inclusion.

(a) *Reality.* $\iota$-reality in the sense of [def-wf-iota-real] is a
condition on the local characteristic polynomials at the closed points,
so $u^*\mathcal G_0$ is an $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$.

(b) *Constituents.* Restriction $u^*$ is exact, and by
[lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective] (4) it carries irreducible lisse
Weil sheaves on $C_0$ to irreducible ones on $U_0$. Hence it carries a
composition series of $\mathcal G_0$ through which $\mathcal W$ occurs
as a successive quotient to a composition series of $u^*\mathcal G_0$,
and $u^*\mathcal W$ is an irreducible constituent of
$u^*\mathcal G_0$.

(c) *Determinant weight.* $\det(u^*\mathcal W)=u^*\det(\mathcal W)$,
and $\det(\mathcal W)$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $a$ with
$\dw_\iota(\mathcal W)=a/r$ by [lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists] and
[def-wf-determinantal-weight]; its restriction is punctually pure of the
same weight $a$ at the closed points of $U_0$, so by the uniqueness in
[lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists] on $U_0$ we get
$\dw_\iota(u^*\mathcal W)=a/r=\dw_\iota(\mathcal W)$.

The local Frobenius $F_x$ on $\mathcal W_{\bar x}$ is the same as on
$(u^*\mathcal W)_{\bar x}$. Therefore it suffices to prove the theorem
for the smooth geometrically connected affine curve $U_0$ and the
$\iota$-real lisse sheaf $u^*\mathcal G_0$: its conclusion at $x$ for
the constituent $u^*\mathcal W$ is the required purity of
$\mathcal W$ of weight $\dw_\iota(\mathcal W)$ at $x$. In Steps 1–4 we
thus assume that $C_0=U_0$ is affine, and write $\mathcal G_0$ for the
sheaf on $U_0$.

Step 1 (reduction to the semisimple case). Replacing $\mathcal G_0$ by its semisimplification does not change the local characteristic polynomials (by the Brauer–Nesbitt argument of [lem-wf-real-semisimplification]), hence changes neither $\iota$-reality in the sense of [def-wf-iota-real] nor the determinant weights of $\mathcal G_0$. The resulting semisimple Weil representation is geometrically semisimple by [lem-mg-normal-restriction-semisimple]. We therefore assume that $\mathcal G_0$ is semisimple, with distinct determinant weights $\gamma_1>\gamma_2>\cdots>\gamma_r$, and write $\mathcal G_0=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}\mathcal G_0(i)$ where $\mathcal G_0(i)$ is the direct sum of the irreducible constituents of determinant weight $\gamma_i$, of total rank $r(i)$.

By [def-rp-weight-blocks], $\mathcal G_0(i)=\mathcal G_0(\gamma_i)$ is the weight block of weight $\gamma_i$, and the decomposition is independent of the choice of decomposition into irreducible summands.

Applying [lem-rp-upper-bound] to $\mathcal G_0$, whose largest determinant weight is $\gamma_1$, gives, at every closed point $x$ and every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_x$ on $\mathcal G_{0,\bar x}$, $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_x^{\gamma_1}$.

The dual sheaf $\mathcal G_0^\vee$ is also $\iota$-real: its local eigenvalue multiset is the inverse multiset by [p-linear-spectra]. Its constituent determinant weights are $-\gamma_i$, because dualizing a determinant line negates its punctual weight by [lem-tw-dual-negation]. Thus its largest determinant weight is $-\gamma_r$, and [lem-rp-upper-bound] applied to the dual gives $|\iota(\alpha^{-1})|^2\le q_x^{-\gamma_r}$, hence $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\ge q_x^{\gamma_r}$.
Step 3 (the estimates for each isotypic part). Fix $n\ge0$ with $r(n+1)>0$ (writing $r(i)=0$ for $i>r$). Put $N:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}r(i)$ and $\mathcal T_0:=\bigwedge^{N+1}\mathcal G_0$.
In the notation of [def-rp-weight-blocks], $N=N_{\gamma_{n+1}}$ and $\sum_{i\le n}r(i)\gamma_i=B_{\gamma_{n+1}}$.

By [cor-mg-det-weight-exterior], the determinant weights of $\mathcal T_0$ are the sums $\sum_i n_i\gamma_i$ with $0\le n_i\le r(i)$ and $\sum_i n_i=N+1$. Since $\gamma_1>\cdots>\gamma_r$, the maximum is $\gamma_{n+1}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}r(i)\gamma_i$, attained at $n_i=r(i)$ for $i\le n$ and $n_{n+1}=1$; every other admissible tuple is strictly smaller. The sheaf $\mathcal T_0$ is $\iota$-real by [lem-rp-exterior-reality], so [lem-rp-upper-bound] gives $|\iota(\lambda)|^2\le q_x^{\gamma_{n+1}+\sum_{i\le n}r(i)\gamma_i}$ for every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F_x$ on $\mathcal T_0$.

For an eigenvalue $\alpha^{(n+1)}_j$ of the $\gamma_{n+1}$ block, the direct-sum decomposition [lem-mg-exterior-direct-sum] contains the summand $\mathcal L=(\det\mathcal G_0(1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\det\mathcal G_0(n))\otimes\mathcal G_0(n+1)$, using the top-exterior-power determinant identification in [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. Its local Frobenius eigenvalues are, by [p-linear-spectra] (top exterior power and tensor product), the products of all eigenvalues of each $\mathcal G_0(i)$, $i\le n$, with one eigenvalue of $\mathcal G_0(n+1)$, and an eigenvalue of a direct summand of $\mathcal T_0$ is one of $\mathcal T_0$. Hence $\lambda=\alpha^{(n+1)}_j\prod_{i=1}^{n}\prod_{j=1}^{r(i)}\alpha^{(i)}_j$ is an eigenvalue of $\mathcal T_0$.

For each $i\le n$, write $\mathcal G_0(i)=\bigoplus_a V_a$ with $V_a$ irreducible of rank $r_a$ and $\dw_\iota(V_a)=\gamma_i$. By [lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists] and [def-wf-determinantal-weight], $\det V_a$ is punctually pure of weight $r_a\gamma_i$, and by [p-linear-spectra] its Frobenius eigenvalue at $x$ is the product of the eigenvalues of $F_x$ on $V_{a,\bar x}$; by [def-weil-punctual-weights] that product has $|\iota(\cdot)|^2=q_x^{r_a\gamma_i}$. The eigenvalues on $\mathcal G_0(i)_{\bar x}$ are the union of those on the $V_{a,\bar x}$, so, the complex absolute value being multiplicative, $\prod_{j=1}^{r(i)}|\iota(\alpha^{(i)}_j)|^2=q_x^{\sum_a r_a\gamma_i}=q_x^{r(i)\gamma_i}$. Substituting this into the bound of the preceding step (all eigenvalues are nonzero, $F_x$ being invertible) yields $|\iota(\alpha^{(n+1)}_j)|^2\le q_x^{\gamma_{n+1}}$ for every $j$.

For the lower bound, apply the same construction to $\mathcal G_0^\vee$, which is semisimple, $\iota$-real and has determinant weights $-\gamma_i$ by the preceding steps. Its decreasing determinant weights are $-\gamma_r>\cdots>-\gamma_1$, and its weight block of weight $-\gamma_i$ in [def-rp-weight-blocks] is the dual of $\mathcal G_0(i)$; the block dual to $\mathcal G_0(n+1)$ is the $(r-n)$-th block, of weight $-\gamma_{n+1}$. Put $N^\vee=\sum_{j=n+2}^{r}r(j)$ and $\mathcal T_0^\vee=\bigwedge^{N^\vee+1}\mathcal G_0^\vee$. By [cor-mg-det-weight-exterior] its largest determinant weight is $-\gamma_{n+1}-\sum_{j\ge n+2}r(j)\gamma_j$, it is $\iota$-real by [lem-rp-exterior-reality], and [lem-rp-upper-bound] bounds its eigenvalues accordingly. The summand $(\bigotimes_{j\ge n+2}\det\mathcal G_0(j)^\vee)\otimes\mathcal G_0(n+1)^\vee$ of [lem-mg-exterior-direct-sum] carries, by [p-linear-spectra], the eigenvalue $\alpha^{-1}\prod_{j\ge n+2}\prod_k(\alpha^{(j)}_k)^{-1}$, and the product over block $j$ has $|\iota(\cdot)|^2=q_x^{-r(j)\gamma_j}$ by the calculation of the preceding step and [lem-tw-dual-negation] (equivalently by inverting it). This gives $|\iota(\alpha^{-1})|^2\le q_x^{-\gamma_{n+1}}$, hence $|\iota(\alpha)|^2\ge q_x^{\gamma_{n+1}}$.

So every eigenvalue satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_x^{\gamma_{n+1}/2}$, which is punctual purity of weight $\gamma_{n+1}$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. The estimate applies to every $n$ with $r(n+1)>0$, so every isotypic part and hence every irreducible constituent is punctually pure of its determinant weight, as asserted.
